title: Beyond the 956: Hubert “Geese” Ausbie, Harlem Globetrotters legend, dies at 88
excerpt: Hubert “Geese” Ausbie, the Harlem Globetrotters legend known as the “Clown Prince of Basketball,” has died at 88. He died November 8, 2026, after 24 years with the Globetrotters, the team announced.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Hubert “Geese” Ausbie, the Harlem Globetrotters legend known as the “Clown Prince of Basketball,” has died at 88.

Ausbie died on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The Harlem Globetrotters announced his death on Monday, November 9.

Born April 25, 1938, in Crescent, Oklahoma, Ausbie starred at Philander Smith College in Little Rock, where he graduated in 1960. He turned down offers from NBA teams — and interest from Major League Baseball’s Chicago Cubs — to join the Globetrotters, earning a spot at a 1961 open tryout in Chicago that drew more than 500 players.

He played for the Globetrotters from 1961 to 1985, 24 years of trick shots, comedy routines and sellout crowds in more than 100 countries, and took over as the team’s lead entertainer when Meadowlark Lemon left in 1978. He later returned as the Globetrotters’ head coach in 1995.

His honors included induction into the Arkansas Sports Hall of Fame in 1990 and the Arkansas Black Hall of Fame in 1995, and the Globetrotters retired his No. 35 jersey in January 2017.

Ausbie was married for 61 years to his wife Awilda, who died in 2020.

Rest in Peace, Geese Ausbie.

Sources: Harlem Globetrotters (official team announcement, November 9, 2026); Cox Media Group; THV11; Encyclopedia of Arkansas.
